# SOP-P2-L4-05 Planned shutdown - Heat Treat line

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-RR01, EQ-P2-L4-HT02, EQ-P2-L4-HP03

Related documents: MM-P2-L4-HT02, SB-1007, SOP-P2-L4-04

Purpose
1. Provide a repeatable, auditable procedure for a planned shutdown of the Heat Treat line to perform maintenance, inspection, and safe isolation of process equipment. This SOP covers mechanical isolation, lubricant inspection, electrical lockout, purge/vent requirements, and preservation of equipment until restart.

Background and scope
2. The Heat Treat line includes the radial ring rolling mill (EQ-P2-L4-RR01), the heat treat furnace module (EQ-P2-L4-HT02), and the hydraulic forging press (EQ-P2-L4-HP03). Planned shutdowns are scheduled to allow alignment, replacement of wear components, lubrication servicing, and to perform safety-critical inspections identified in MM-P2-L4-HT02 and SB-1007. This SOP applies to maintenance and engineering personnel responsible for those tasks and ends at the point of hand-back to operations for restart, which is governed by SOP-P2-L4-04.

Preconditions (must be verified before initiating step 1)
3.1. Work order or shutdown authorization is present and signed by Maintenance Supervisor.  
3.2. Production schedule confirmed and line isolated from upstream/downstream processes.  
3.3. Notify operations and safety teams per plant communication protocol.  
3.4. Required spares and consumables staged per MM-P2-L4-HT02.  
3.5. The lubricant part number for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) is CFW-LUB-723.  
3.6. The lubricant part number for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is CFW-LUB-450.

PPE and barriers
4.1. Minimum PPE: safety glasses, hearing protection, gloves rated for mechanical work, steel-toe boots, and high-visibility vest. Additional PPE such as arc-rated clothing or respirator must be used when performing the specific task that requires it per local hazard assessment.  
4.2. Use barricades and tagout signs to physically isolate the work area from pedestrian routes.  
4.3. Hot work permits and confined space permits must be obtained and co-located with the work package if applicable.

Shutdown procedure (numbered operational steps)
5.1. Notify affected personnel and post signage at access points. Confirm communications with operations lead. Rationale: ensures single point of responsibility and prevents inadvertent energy application during shutdown.  
5.2. Stop production feed and drain inventory from the Heat Treat line per process team instructions. Verify zero material at machine infeed and outfeed points. Rationale: prevents material entrapment and enables safe access.  
5.3. Isolate energy sources: electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, and process utilities feeding EQ-P2-L4-RR01, EQ-P2-L4-HT02, and EQ-P2-L4-HP03. Apply lockout/tagout devices according to company LOTO standard. Rationale: eliminates hazard from stored or residual energy.  
5.4. Depressurize and vent hydraulic and pneumatic systems. Verify pressure gauges indicate zero where present. Note: use purge lines provided on the equipment. Rationale: prevents accidental motion or release during maintenance.  
5.5. Disconnect and cap process utility connections to EQ-P2-L4-HT02 if it will be opened for inspection. Follow SB-1007 for furnace purge and inerting sequences when furnace access is required. Rationale: avoids combustion and contamination hazards.  
5.6. Secure mechanical locks or blocks on moving components for EQ-P2-L4-RR01 and EQ-P2-L4-HP03 to prevent unintentional movement. Rationale: positive mechanical restraint is required in addition to energy isolation.  
5.7. Inventory and document current lubricant state at all lubrication points on EQ-P2-L4-RR01 and EQ-P2-L4-HP03. Replace or top-up lubricants using the approved lubricants: the lubricant part number for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) is CFW-LUB-723; the lubricant part number for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is CFW-LUB-450. Rationale: prevents premature wear and documents compliance with MM-P2-L4-HT02. Example: record bearing location, existing oil level, and new oil batch/part number.  
5.8. Perform required inspections and maintenance activities per the maintenance work order and MM-P2-L4-HT02 tasks list. Document torque values, clearances, and part replacements on the work order where applicable. Rationale: ensures maintenance meets design intent and is traceable.  
5.9. If welding, grinding, or hot work is performed on or near EQ-P2-L4-HT02, obtain hot work permit and follow SB-1007 procedures for fire watch and inerting. Rationale: control of ignition sources near heat treat equipment is critical.  
5.10. After maintenance is complete, remove tools and foreign material. Conduct a housekeeping inspection of the work area. Rationale: reduces foreign object risk during restart.

Pre-start checks and hand-back to operations
6.1. Reassemble guards and verify interlocks operate per SOP-P2-L4-04. Rationale: protects operators during startup and normal operation.  
6.2. Remove lockout/tagout devices only after verification that all personnel are clear and the maintenance lead agrees. Restore utilities in the sequence identified in the equipment manufacturer guidance and MM-P2-L4-HT02.  
6.3. Perform low-speed functional tests and observe for abnormal noise, leaks, or alarms. Escalate any anomalies to Engineering. Rationale: incremental testing reduces stress on systems and catches issues early.  
6.4. Complete the equipment test checklist and forward to Operations and Maintenance records.

Records to keep
7.1. Signed shutdown authorization and work order.  
7.2. LOTO tags and log showing responsible individuals.  
7.3. Lubrication records documenting that EQ-P2-L4-RR01 used CFW-LUB-723 and EQ-P2-L4-HP03 used CFW-LUB-450, including batch/lot numbers where available.  
7.4. Inspection reports and parts replaced, referenced to MM-P2-L4-HT02 work items.  
7.5. Hot work permits and fire watch logs if applicable per SB-1007.  
7.6. Final hand-back sign-off form per SOP-P2-L4-04.

Examples and notes
8.1. Example entry for lubrication record: "EQ-P2-L4-RR01 bearing A: drained, inspected, refilled with CFW-LUB-723, batch 12345, tech J. Smith." Use the exact lubricant part numbers as required.  
8.2. Use the related documents for task-specific checklists: MM-P2-L4-HT02 for mechanical tolerances, SB-1007 for hot work and furnace safety, SOP-P2-L4-04 for startup and safety interlock verification.

Sign-off (to be completed at the end of the shutdown)
9.1. Maintenance Lead name / signature / date.  
9.2. Operations Lead name / signature / date.  
9.3. Safety Representative name / signature / date.

Revision control
10. All changes to this SOP must be submitted through document control with reference to MM-P2-L4-HT02 and SB-1007 where applicable.
